We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene). 3) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or aniline derivative). Then break alkene to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid. So reverse: the unsaturated acid precursor is aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid. So we can split the unsaturated acid fragment (C= C -C(=O)N...) Wait the unsaturated acid is part of target: /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the target has amide: C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide formation step is between the unsaturated acid (C= C -C(=O) ) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: break amide to give unsaturated acid (C= C -C(=O)OH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner: give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc...?) Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring c2ccc(... )cc2 (the sulfonyl phenyl). The unsaturated acid is attached to that phenyl via the double bond: /C=C/ attached to the phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (ring B) has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring with an aldehyde at that position (i.e., c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So Doebner: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl. So we need malonic acid as other precursor.

Third step: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide linking the first phenyl (ring A) with sulfonyl chloride and an amine (the phenyl B). Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl A (para-methyl phenyl) and to phenyl B (the one with side chain). So sulfonamide formed from sulfonyl chloride (derived from phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride) reacting with an amine (para-methyl aniline). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl B and aniline (para-methyl aniline). So overall route:

Step 1 (retro): target -> break amide: product1 = unsaturated acid (phenyl B side chain) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is between unsaturated acid carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we get unsaturated acid (phenyl B with side chain) and aniline (para-aminophenyl? Wait the aniline is attached to the amide nitrogen, not the sulfonamide. The amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B side chain and to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amine is an aniline (aniline with para amino? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). So step 1: unsaturated acid + aniline.

Step 2 (retro): unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (phenyl B with aldehyde) + malonic acid.

Step 3 (retro): sulfonyl chloride (phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride) + para-methyl aniline (the other phenyl A) to give sulfonamide linking them. Wait we also need phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride; but phenyl B currently has sulfonyl attached to it (the sulfonamide). In the target, phenyl B is attached to sulfonyl group (S(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl A). Actually the sulfonamide is between phenyl A (para-methyl phenyl) and phenyl B (the one with side chain). So breaking sulfonamide gives sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl B and aniline (para-methyl aniline). So we need sulfonyl chloride precursor: phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride (i.e., Cl-SO2-PhB). That phenyl B also has the side chain (unsaturated acid). So after step 2 we have phenyl B with unsaturated acid (but not sulfonyl). Wait step 2 gave phenyl B with unsaturated acid (no sulfonyl). But step 3 requires phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride. So we need to combine steps: maybe order is: first sulfonamide formation (connect phenyl A and phenyl B with sulfonyl chloride). Then Doebner modification on phenyl B (which already has sulfonyl attached) to install unsaturated acid. Then amide formation to attach aniline.

Thus retrosynthetic order (reverse) is: target -> break amide (step 1) -> unsaturated acid attached to phenyl B with sulfonyl attached to phenyl A + aniline. Then break unsaturated acid via Doebner (step 2) -> aromatic aldehyde attached to phenyl B with sulfonyl attached to phenyl A + malonic acid. Then break sulfonamide (step 3) -> sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl B (with aldehyde) + para-methyl aniline (the amine). So three steps.

We need to find templates for each transformation.

We have template for sulfonamide formation (retro: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide). In search results earlier, template_id 733 seems to be sulfonamide formation (Cl-SO2-Ph + aniline). Let's retrieve template 733.
